settings.name: Walnut Dog Rescue
settings.tagline: Rescue, care and a second chance for every dog.
settings.charity: Walnut Dog Rescue is a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization. EIN 00-0000000.
settings.feeNote: Every adoption includes vaccines, spay or neuter, a microchip, a first vet check and a bag of food.
settings.pledgeText: Mail a check to Walnut Dog Rescue, 48 Mill Pond Road, Hollis Ferry, or bring cash or card to the front desk during visiting hours. Write your pledge number on the check so we can thank you.
settings.wishList:
Large-breed dog food
Washable dog beds
Leashes and martingale collars
Chew toys for strong chewers
Old towels and blankets
Puppy pads
Peanut butter, xylitol-free

dogs.name: Biscuit
dogs.story:
Biscuit came to us when his family moved overseas. He is a big, soft-mouthed goofball who carries a toy everywhere and greets every visitor with a full-body wag.

He walks nicely on a leash, rides calmly in the car and settles on his bed in the evening. He would love a family with time for long walks and a yard for fetch.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Juniper
dogs.story:
Juniper is clever, loyal and a little serious until she knows you. Then she is your shadow, checking where you are and bringing you her rope toy.

She needs an active home that enjoys training and hiking. She plays well with confident dogs but chases cats, so a cat-free home is a must.
traits: Best as the only cat-free home

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Pepper
dogs.story:
Pepper has more energy than our whole kennel staff put together. She runs, jumps, catches and then asks for more.

With a daily job, like agility, fetch or long runs, she is a sweet, attentive companion who leans against your legs at the end of the day.
traits: Learns a trick in a day

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Mabel
dogs.story:
Mabel and her sister Sadie arrived together from a farm that could no longer keep them. Mabel is the talker of the two and howls a little song when she sees her leash.

They must be adopted together. They are house-trained, gentle with children and happiest snuggled on one dog bed.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Otis
dogs.story:
Otis has never met a person he did not like. He wiggles from nose to tail, bounces when he is excited and then falls asleep snoring on the nearest sofa.

He needs a little help with jumping up, but he is learning fast and will sit politely for a treat.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Hazel
dogs.story:
Hazel is a lap dog in a sturdy body. She leans in for every hug and rolls over for belly rubs within a minute of meeting you.

She has an adoption pending with a family in Hollis Ferry. If it falls through we will update this page.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Rocket
dogs.story:
Rocket is a chatty, handsome boy with ice-blue eyes. He howls hello, talks back and runs like the wind.

He needs a home with a tall, secure fence and people who enjoy long walks in any weather. He gets along with other dogs and loves a playmate.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Daisy
dogs.story:
Daisy is sunshine on four legs. She is staying with one of our foster families, who say she is perfect with their cat and their two boys.

Meetings are arranged through our adoption team. Apply and we will introduce you.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Gus
dogs.needs: Ear drops twice a day until healed.
dogs.story: Gus is recovering from ear surgery and will be ready for adoption soon.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.
Ear drops twice a day for 14 days.

dogs.name: Luna
dogs.story:
Luna is tiny but brave. In her foster home she has taken charge of the sofa and the family's older cat.

She would do best with adults or older children who will let her warm up at her own pace.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Theo
dogs.story:
Theo is a curly, happy boy who greets everyone like an old friend. He sheds very little and loves being brushed.

He walks well on a leash and is learning to stay. He would fit into almost any loving home.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Willow
dogs.story:
Willow retired from racing and now prefers soft blankets. She sprints around the yard for five minutes and then naps for five hours.

She is gentle, quiet and polite in the house. A small-animal test is needed before she meets cats.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Bear
dogs.story:
Bear has been with us for over four months, longer than any other dog. He is a calm, gentle giant who leans his whole weight on you for a hug.

He needs an adult home without cats, and a little patience while he settles. He will pay you back with loyalty for the rest of his life.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Penny
dogs.story: Penny loves to burrow in blankets.
dogs.happyTail: Penny now has three dog beds and a tunnel of blankets under the dining table. She walks to the park every morning with the kids and barks at exactly one squirrel.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Scout
dogs.story:
Scout is a speckled bundle of brains and stamina. He loves trails, puzzle feeders and learning new tricks.

He can be nervous with very young children who run around, so a home with older kids or adults is best.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Nala
dogs.story:
Nala is a short-legged comedian with enormous ears. She herds the other dogs at playtime and smiles at everyone she meets.

She is house-trained, crate-trained and gets along with dogs, cats and children.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Duke
dogs.story:
Duke is a huge, mellow boy who takes up the whole kennel and would prefer a sofa. He moves slowly, sighs happily and loves gentle pats.

He needs a foster or forever home soon because the kennel is hard on his joints.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Rosie
dogs.story: Rosie was surrendered with matted fur.
dogs.happyTail: Rosie's coat grew back soft and shiny. She goes to the groomer every six weeks and comes home wiggling with pride. She sleeps at the foot of the bed.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Milo
dogs.story:
Milo is a scruffy little terrier with a big sense of fun. He collects toys in his bed and shows them off to every visitor.

He is friendly with other dogs and walks beautifully on a leash.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Ziggy
dogs.story:
Ziggy is a spotty athlete who would love a running partner. He plays in the hose, chases balls and still has energy left.

He is good with dogs and kids, and he is working on calm greetings.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Clover
dogs.story:
Clover is a striking young dog with one blue eye and one brown. She is smart, eager and learns new cues in a single session.

She needs an active family that enjoys training. She is great with kids, dogs and cats.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Tank
dogs.story: Tank was found on a hot day.
dogs.happyTail: Tank has a cooling mat on the porch and a fan in summer. He takes three short walks a day and has become the unofficial greeter at Marcus's bike shop.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Ginger
dogs.story:
Ginger has a fox-like face and a cat-like attitude: affectionate on her terms and endlessly curious.

She is house-trained and fine alone for a few hours. A calm home with adults would suit her best.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Bruno
dogs.story: Bruno loves to swim.
dogs.happyTail: Bruno swims in the lake every weekend and carries his tennis ball like a trophy. The kids taught him to ring a bell when he wants to go out.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Lady
dogs.story:
Lady is ten years young, with a gray muzzle and a heart of gold. Her family could no longer care for her after a move, and she is a little confused by kennel life.

She is house-trained, quiet and happy with short walks and long naps. Our senior fee is reduced to help her find a home quickly.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.
Senior blood panel normal. Mild arthritis, joint supplement started.

dogs.name: Pip
dogs.story: Pip never stops.
dogs.happyTail: Pip runs agility on Thursdays and has two ribbons already. At home he finally learned to nap, as long as it is on Hannah's lap.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Ollie
dogs.story:
Ollie is a distinguished gentleman with a magnificent beard. He keeps an eye on the house and lets you know when the mail arrives.

A family has applied for Ollie and a home visit is booked.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Sadie
dogs.story:
Sadie is the quiet half of a bonded pair with her sister Mabel. She follows Mabel everywhere and is happiest curled up beside her.

The two must be adopted together for one adoption fee. They are gentle with children, dogs and cats.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Koda
dogs.story: Koda arrived this week and is settling in.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Winnie
dogs.story: Winnie loves laps.
dogs.happyTail: Winnie has a pink bed by the window and a weekly brushing appointment with Eleanor. They watch the birds together every afternoon.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Ranger
dogs.story:
Ranger is an athletic, loyal dog who loves to hike. He is watchful with strangers at first and then becomes a goofy companion.

He needs an experienced owner who will keep up with his training. He is wonderful with confident dogs.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Maple
dogs.story:
Maple is a four-month-old puppy with ears she has not grown into yet. She is with a foster family learning house manners and puppy socialization.

She will be a medium to large adult. Puppy classes are a must, and we include one free class with her adoption.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Bean
dogs.story:
Bean is a snorting, snoring, cuddly little man. In his foster home he follows people from room to room and naps in any lap available.

He needs a cool home in summer and short walks. He is great with everyone.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

dogs.name: Cooper
dogs.story:
Cooper is a fluffy, gentle giant who adores children and will sit beside a stroller for as long as you like.

He sheds a lot and needs regular brushing. He loves cool weather and sleeping on the porch.

health.note: Intake exam. Healthy weight, clear eyes and ears.

events.title: Saturday Open House
events.place: Walnut Dog Rescue, 48 Mill Pond Road
events.text: Meet our adoptable dogs in the play yard, talk to the adoption team and take a tour of the kennels. Families and well-behaved dogs welcome.

events.title: Volunteer Orientation
events.text: New volunteers start here: a tour, safety basics and how to sign up for shifts. Required before your first shift.

events.title: Adoption Day at the Farmers Market
events.place: Hollis Ferry Farmers Market, Town Green
events.text: Ten of our dogs come to the Saturday market. Say hello, ask questions and start an application on the spot.

events.title: Puppy Manners Class
events.text: A friendly first class for puppies under six months: sit, come, loose-leash walking and calm greetings. Free for dogs adopted from us.

events.title: Howl-o-ween Costume Walk
events.text: Our biggest fundraiser of the fall: a one-mile costume walk, a pet photo booth and treats for everyone. All proceeds go to the medical fund.

events.title: Summer Open House
events.place: Walnut Dog Rescue, 48 Mill Pond Road
events.text: Meet our adoptable dogs, tour the kennels and enjoy lemonade in the shade.

blocks.title: Every dog deserves a family.
blocks.text: We rescue dogs in and around {town}, give them medical care and a safe place to stay, and match them with homes that fit. Adopt, foster, volunteer or give: every bit helps.
blocks.label: Meet the dogs

items.title: Adopt
items.text: Find a dog who fits your life. One application, a meet and greet and a home visit.
items.label: Meet the dogs

items.title: Foster
items.text: Open your home for a few weeks. We cover food, supplies and vet care.
items.label: Become a foster

items.title: Volunteer
items.text: Walk dogs, help at events, take photos or drive to the vet.
items.label: Sign up to help

items.title: Donate
items.text: Every gift pays for food, vaccines and surgery for dogs in our care.
items.label: Give today

blocks.title: Waiting the longest
blocks.text: These dogs have been with us the longest or find kennel life hard. A foster home for a few weeks would change everything.
blocks.label: Foster a dog

blocks.title: A small rescue with a big yard
blocks.text:
{name} started in 2009 with three volunteers and a borrowed barn. Today our team of staff, volunteers and foster families cares for about 40 dogs at a time and finds homes for more than 200 a year.

We never put a healthy dog to sleep for space.
blocks.label: Visit the shelter

blocks.kicker: Give a dog a good day
blocks.title: Your gift goes straight to the dogs
blocks.text: $25 feeds a dog for two weeks. $100 covers vaccines and a microchip. $250 pays for a spay or neuter.
blocks.label: Donate

blocks.title: Adopting a dog, step by step
blocks.text: Fill in one application and our adoption team will call you within two days. We meet you and the dog, visit your home and help you get ready for the big day.
blocks.label: Start your application

items.title: Apply online
items.text: Choose a dog, or leave it open and tell us about your home. It takes about ten minutes.

items.title: We call you
items.text: Our adoption team calls within two days to talk about your routine and answer questions.

items.title: Meet and greet
items.text: Visit the dog at the shelter or in their foster home. Bring everyone who lives with you, dogs included.

items.title: Home visit
items.text: A short, friendly visit to see where the dog will live and to help you dog-proof.

items.title: Adoption day
items.text: Sign the adoption agreement, pay the fee and take your new friend home with a starter kit.

blocks.title: Adoption fees
blocks.text: Bonded pairs go home together for one fee. Some dogs have their own fee on their page.

items.title: Do I need a fenced yard?
items.text: Not for every dog. Some dogs need one, and their page says so. Many of our dogs live happily in apartments with daily walks.

items.title: Can I adopt if I rent?
items.text: Yes. We ask for your landlord's contact so we can confirm dogs are allowed, including any size limits.

items.title: How long does it take?
items.text: Usually one to two weeks from application to adoption day, depending on visits and references.

items.title: What if it does not work out?
items.text: Call us. We always take our dogs back, at any age, and help you find the right next step.

items.title: I already have a dog. Can they meet?
items.text: Please bring them. We arrange a calm introduction on neutral ground before any adoption.

blocks.title: Lend a dog your sofa
blocks.text: Fostering gives a dog a break from the kennel, and gives us a better picture of how they live in a home. We provide food, supplies, vet care and a 24-hour helpline. You provide a couch and some love.
blocks.label: Sign up to foster

items.title: We provide
items.text:
Food, bowls, leash, crate and toys
All vet care, medicine and transport
A 24-hour helpline and a foster coordinator
Training tips and a free class
Help finding the right adopter

items.title: You provide
items.text:
A safe, loving home for a few weeks or more
Walks, play and patience
Rides to vet visits and meet and greets when you can
Notes and photos so adopters get to know the dog

items.title: How long?
items.text:
Up to 2 weeks: weekend breaks and recovery after surgery
2 to 8 weeks: puppies, shy dogs and house training
2 months or more: seniors and dogs who wait the longest

blocks.title: Dogs who would love a break from the kennel
Nora, a foster since 2024
blocks.text: We said yes to two weeks with a dog recovering from surgery. She taught our kids to be gentle, and waving her off to her new family was the best kind of sad.

blocks.title: Foster sign-up
blocks.text: Our foster coordinator calls every new foster and books a short home visit before your first dog.

blocks.title: Give a few hours, change a dog's week
blocks.text: Volunteers walk dogs, clean kennels, take photos, drive dogs to the vet and help at events. Every volunteer starts with a free orientation.
blocks.label: Sign up to volunteer

items.title: Dog walking
items.text: Take dogs out for walks on our trails and around the neighborhood.

items.title: Socializing and play
items.text: Sit with shy dogs, run playgroups and help puppies meet new people.

items.title: Kennel care
items.text: Clean kennels, wash bowls and do laundry so the dogs live in a fresh space.

items.title: Adoption events
items.text: Help at open houses and adoption days: set up, greet visitors, handle dogs.

items.title: Transport
items.text: Drive dogs to vet visits, foster homes and adoption events.

items.title: Photos and social media
items.text: Take the photos and short videos that get dogs noticed online.

items.title: Fundraising
items.text: Help plan our walk, bake sale and holiday drive, or ask local shops to help.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text:
• Volunteers are 18 or older. Teens 14 to 17 are welcome with a parent.
  • Everyone joins a free 90-minute orientation first.
  • We ask for two shifts a month, booked by our volunteer coordinator.
  • Closed-toe shoes, clothes that can get muddy and a love of dogs.

blocks.title: Come and meet us
blocks.text: Open houses, adoption days, classes and fundraisers. Reserve a place so we know how many treats to bring.
A Saturday open house in the play yard.

blocks.title: Give a dog a good day
blocks.text: We are funded by people like you. Pledge a gift online, then send it by check, in person or by bank transfer.

blocks.title: Home at last
blocks.text: Every adoption starts with someone taking a chance. Here are a few of the dogs who went home recently, in their families' words.

blocks.title: Write the next happy tail
blocks.text: Our dogs are waiting for a family right now. Meet them, or open your home for a few weeks.
blocks.label: Meet the dogs

blocks.title: Visit, call or write
blocks.text: Our kennels are open to visitors during visiting hours. Come and meet the dogs, no appointment needed.

blocks.title: Send us a message
blocks.text: Call us first. If you can, keep the dog somewhere safe and check for a tag. We scan for microchips for free during visiting hours.
